# W2 -- sys_mmapper

Branch explore/w2 from main HEAD 40a0597.

Task: log every sys_mmapper call during RDR boot with arguments and returns; audit
against refs/rpcs3/rpcs3/Emu/Cell/lv2/sys_mmapper.cpp; unit tests per deviation;
fix what differs.

## Build note -- the shipped out-rdr/spu was generated by a branch that is not main

First build of this worktree at main HEAD 40a0597 failed in the SPU generated
sources, not in anything W2 changed:

    /root/Dev/ps3base2/out-rdr/spu/spu_001.cpp:7:16: error: no member named 'base' in 'spu::Context'
    /root/Dev/ps3base2/out-rdr/spu/spu_001.cpp:8:40: error: no member named 'base' in 'spu::Context'
    ... (repeated; fatal error: too many errors emitted, stopping now)
    FAILED: CMakeFiles/ps3base_spu.dir/root/Dev/ps3base2/out-rdr/spu/spu_001.cpp.o

out-rdr/spu is timestamped 13:38 today and emits `c.pc = ((c.base + N) & PC_MASK)`,
which is the content-based-dispatch form from branch explore/u4
(`git grep 'c.base' explore/u4 -- recomp/spu/codegen.py` -> emit_block_base at
line 212). explore/u4 is NOT an ancestor of main (`git merge-base --is-ancestor
explore/u4 main` fails), and main's recomp/spu/codegen.py emits absolute
`c.pc = 0x...` with no `base` member in runtime/include/spu/context.h.

Regenerated with main's own codegen from the same captured block set, into this
worktree so the shared tree is not disturbed:

    PS3BASE_PROFILE= python3 recomp/spu/codegen.py /root/Dev/wt-W2/out-W2/spu '/root/Dev/ps3base2/out-rdr/gen/blocks/run*.bin'
    52680 blocks, 738000 instructions, 132 files, 5699 regions covering 16006 blocks,
    7606 direct regions covering 26191 blocks

and the build was configured with -DGOWA_SPU_GENERATED_DIR=/root/Dev/wt-W2/out-W2/spu.
## Measurement 1 -- the sys_mmapper call table during RDR boot (main HEAD 40a0597 + call logging)

Run:

    cd /root/Dev/wt-W2 && ln -sfn /root/Dev/ps3base2/out-rdr out-rdr
    Xvfb :931 -screen 0 1280x720x24 &
    nohup setsid env DISPLAY=:931 XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/0 \
      PS3BASE_DISC_DIR=/root/Dev/rdr-port/vfs/dev_bdvd PS3BASE_LOG=info \
      timeout 130 /root/Dev/wt-W2/build-31/ps3base --no-launcher > /tmp/W2.log 2>&1 < /dev/null &

Every sys_mmapper entry logs its five raw argument registers and its return
value on channel 'mmapper'. The complete set of calls the title makes in 130 s:

    I   0.809811 mmapper: sys_mmapper_allocate_address r3=0x10000000 r4=0xf0 r5=0x10000000 r6=0xd004fa94 r7=0x0 -> 0x0
    I   0.809819 mmapper: allocate_address 0x10000000 -> 0x40000000
    I   0.809827 mmapper: sys_mmapper_allocate_address r3=0x10000000 r4=0xf0 r5=0x10000000 r6=0xd004fa94 r7=0x0 -> 0x0
    I   0.809834 mmapper: allocate_address 0x10000000 -> 0x50000000
    I   0.809843 mmapper: sys_mmapper_allocate_address r3=0x10000000 r4=0xf0 r5=0x10000000 r6=0xd004fa94 r7=0x0 -> 0x0
    I   0.809857 mmapper: allocate_address 0x10000000 -> 0x60000000

    $ grep -o 'sys_mmapper_[a-z_]*' /tmp/W2.log | sort | uniq -c
          3 sys_mmapper_allocate_address

That is the whole table: **three calls to sys_mmapper_allocate_address and
nothing else**, all from PPU thread 0x1000004 (log tid 2765229), all with
size 0x10000000, flags 0xf0, alignment 0x10000000, out pointer 0xd004fa94,
all returning CELL_OK with a 256 MiB area.

The surrounding lines name the caller's intent:

    I   0.809709 tty: [0] [STARTUP] Restricting 211968k heap to 69632k+3072k+112640k=185344k.
    I   0.809898 tty: [0] [STARTUP] Allocating 181M
    I   0.809911 vm: region 2 placed at 0x70000000

so the three areas are the title's three heap regions and the 181M heap is a
sys_vm_memory_map (syscall 300), not an mmapper call.

The sysPrxForUser wrappers that would reach the other five entries DO exist as
imports in the lifted table (`/root/Dev/ps3base2/out-rdr/ppu/table.cpp:77336-77429`:
sys_mmapper_free_memory 0x409AD939, sys_mmapper_unmap_memory 0x4643BA6E,
sys_mmapper_allocate_memory_from_container 0x70258515,
sys_mmapper_allocate_memory 0xB257540B, sys_mmapper_map_memory 0xDC578057),
and none of them is reached before the title stops. `PS3BASE_RESOLVE_LOG=1`
reports zero unresolved imports, so this is not a missing-symbol artefact: the
title genuinely does not get to the shared-memory path in the first 130 s.

### What the audit therefore has to be about

The measured table is thin, so the deviations that matter are not the ones RDR
exercises today -- they are the ones it will exercise when the SPURS abort is
fixed and the title gets past startup. The audit below reads each of the eight
implemented handlers against refs/rpcs3/rpcs3/Emu/Cell/lv2/sys_mmapper.cpp and
records every place the two disagree.
## Measurement 2 -- the audit, the deviations, and the fixes

runtime/src/lv2/mmapper.cpp was read line by line against
refs/rpcs3/rpcs3/Emu/Cell/lv2/sys_mmapper.cpp. Eleven deviations were found.
Each is fixed, and tests/mmapper_conformance.cpp has one check per deviation
(D-numbers below); the test drives the logic functions directly, with the real
address allocator linked, so the image-overlap rule is exercised rather than
assumed.

### Deviation table

| # | syscall | RPCS3 says (file:line) | this tree did | fixed to |
|---|---------|------------------------|---------------|----------|
| D1 | allocate_address | size % 0x10000000 -> EALIGN (:214-217) | same | same |
| D2 | allocate_address | size > u32 max -> ENOMEM (:219-222) | absent; size cast to u32 and truncated | ENOMEM |
| D3 | allocate_address | alignment 0 means 0x10000000 (:226-229) | same | same |
| D4 | allocate_address | page size must be 0/0x400/0x200 else EINVAL (:231-243) | absent -- any flag accepted | EINVAL |
| D5 | allocate_address | page-fault notify needs RAW_SPU or SPU_THR (:245-251) | absent | EINVAL |
| D6 | allocate_address | SPU_THR + notify is legal | n/a | accepted |
| D7 | allocate_address | align must be 0x10000000/0x20000000/0x40000000/0x80000000 else EALIGN (:253-273) | absent -- any align passed to reserve_slot | EALIGN |
| D12 | free_address | addr outside 0x20000000..0xC0000000 -> EINVAL (:652-655) | absent | EINVAL |
| D13 | free_address | addr not an area -> EINVAL (:663-666) | same answer by accident (erase returned 0) | explicit |
| D16 | allocate_shared_memory | size 0 -> EALIGN (:304-307) | same | same |
| D17/18 | allocate_shared_memory | granularity 0/0x400 -> 1M, 0x200 -> 64K (:310-335) | page from (flags & 0xF00) == 0x200, so 0x100 (4K) fell through to 1M | granularity switch; 0x100 -> EINVAL |
| D19 | allocate_shared_memory | unknown granularity -> EINVAL (:331-334) | silently 1M | EINVAL |
| D24-29 | allocate_shared_memory | create_lv2_shm honours ipc_key and the 0xc000/0x8000 create mode (:188-206) | key ignored entirely -- two guests agreeing on a key got two heaps | keyed map; EEXIST / reuse / EPERM on size mismatch / ESRCH |
| D36 | map_shared_memory | mem.align < area page -> EINVAL (:772-775) | returned EALIGN for both this and the address case | EINVAL |
| D37 | map_shared_memory | addr % page -> EALIGN (:777-780) | same | same |
| D40 | map_shared_memory | counter++, several mappings allowed (:798) | one mapped_at, so a SECOND mapping of the same object returned EBUSY | counter; N mappings |
| D46 | map_shared_memory | one utils::shm per lv2_memory, so a write through one mapping is seen by the next map (:46-54, :787) | zero-fill on every map; data lost on unmap | object-owned buffer, copied in on map and out on unmap |
| D47 | free_shared_memory | counter != 0 -> EBUSY (:726-729) | EBUSY while the single mapped_at was set | EBUSY while any mapping exists |
| D54 | search_and_map | start_addr must BE the area base (:838) | only "inside the area" | exact base required |
| D55 | search_and_map | mem.align < page -> EALIGN here, unlike map EINVAL (:850-855) | returned EINVAL | EALIGN (asymmetry preserved deliberately) |
| D67 | change_address_access_right | returns CELL_OK, todo-logged (:637-644) | not registered at all -- ENOSYS | CELL_OK |
| D68-70 | allocate_fixed_address | maps 0xB0000000+0x10000000, EEXIST if already done (:276-288) | not registered at all -- ENOSYS | CELL_OK / EEXIST |
| D31 | free_shared_memory | unmapped object frees; a second free is ESRCH | same | same |
| D43 | unmap_shared_memory | always writes *mem_id, then counter-- (:952-956) | wrote it only when non-zero | always |

Two entries were unimplemented entirely -- sys_mmapper_allocate_fixed_address (326)
and sys_mmapper_change_address_access_right (336) -- so both returned ENOSYS
"the feature is not yet implemented" for operations the console performs.
That is the failure mode AGENTS.md names: sys_fs_chmod, sys_fs_utime,
sys_net_infoctl and sys_net_bnet_sysctl were made to refuse things RPCS3 accepts,
libnet then initialised against a socket layer that was up and a stack nobody
had built, and the title went from 7081 flips to zero.

### A defect the audit exposed in the shared-memory model

The old module kept one mapped_at per object and zero-filled guest memory on
every map. That is wrong in two directions at once: a second mapping of the same
object was refused with EBUSY (which no console does), and a write made through
one mapping vanished the moment it was unmapped, so a ring buffer shared between
two threads would read back zeroes. lv2_memory::shm in RPCS3 is one buffer with
a reference count (:46-54, :782-798), which is what makes the second mapping see
the first one data. The rewrite keeps that buffer on the object.

## The generated syscall table was stale, and the generator could not see MMAPPER_SYSCALL

tools/lv2/gen_syscall_table.py marks a syscall implemented by finding
LV2_SYSCALL(<num>, in runtime/src/lv2/. The logging wrapper this task added
registers through MMAPPER_SYSCALL, which the pattern did not match, so
regenerating would have flipped the eight mmapper entries back to unimplemented
while they ran. The pattern now accepts both macros.

Regenerating also found eleven entries that were already stale on main -- the
handlers existed and the table said 0:

    { 300, "sys_vm_memory_map", 0 },                         -> 1
    { 302, "sys_vm_append_memory", 0 },                      -> 1
    { 303, "sys_vm_return_memory", 0 },                      -> 1
    { 306, "sys_vm_touch", 0 },                              -> 1
    { 312, "sys_vm_get_statistics", 0 },                     -> 1
    { 326, "sys_mmapper_allocate_fixed_address", 0 },        -> 1
    { 336, "sys_mmapper_change_address_access_right", 0 },   -> 1
    { 722, "sys_net_infoctl", 0 },                           -> 1
    { 725, "sys_net_bnet_sysctl", 0 },                       -> 1
    { 815, "sys_fs_utime", 0 },                              -> 1
    { 834, "sys_fs_chmod", 0 },                              -> 1

so the coverage number this tree reports was understated by eleven throughout.
After regeneration: gen_syscall_table: 451 syscalls listed, 191 implemented (42.4%).

# W3 -- the library inventory: libresc, libspurs_jq, libfiber, libfs, libsync2, libsail

Question: for each of the six, does RDR import it, and is it served LLE, HLE, or not at all?

## 0. The two resolutions the runtime can take, from the code

`runtime/src/ppu_runtime.cpp:179` `resolve()`:

    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < image::export_count; i++) {
        const image::ExportEntry& e = image::exports[i];
        if (e.nid == imp.nid && std::strcmp(e.module, imp.module) == 0 && loader::image_loaded(e.image))
            return i;                       // LLE: a lifted firmware image exports it
    }
    if (hle::Fn fn = hle::find(imp.module, imp.name)) { slot.hle = fn; return kHle; }
    ... return kNone;                        // neither: a call here returns nothing

An import is therefore served **LLE** iff some loaded image's export table has the
same (module, NID) pair; **HLE** iff a runtime handler is registered under that
(module, name); **not at all** otherwise.

| 0xf035 | CELL_SYSMODULE_SYSUTIL_NP_TROPHY | yes (sceNpTrophy) |

**Not one of the 11 ids is 0x1d (SAIL), 0x1f (RESC), 0x50 (SPURS_JQ) or 0x55
(SYNC2).** The dynamic table is id-free for all four, so there is nothing to
lift for the title's benefit.

### 8.3 Export verification -- `tools/check_lle_exports.py`

A module in the image table can still be useless: the lifter may drop an export,
or lift a descriptor without lifting the code it points at. Both faults are
silent -- `resolve()` finds no export, or finds one whose opd reads a code word
with no lifted function, and the call goes to a null dispatch slot.

The checker joins the PRX's own export table against the generated
`exports[]`/`functions[]` and requires, per export: the (module, NID) is present,
the opd is non-zero and equal, and the descriptor's FIRST word -- the code
address, the same word `ppu_runtime.cpp` loads with `code = ld32(base, e.opd)` --
is an entry in `functions[]`. A code word that is not inside an image's text is
skipped, because exports like `sys_prx_version` are data (0x00010001), not
descriptors.

```
$ python3 tools/check_lle_exports.py out-w3/ppu/table.cpp \
    out-w3/gen/reloc/libresc.elf cellResc \
    out-w3/gen/reloc/libspurs_jq.elf cellSpursJq \
    out-w3/gen/reloc/libsail.elf cellSail \
    out-w3/gen/reloc/libfiber.elf cellFiber \
    out-w3/gen/reloc/libfs.elf sys_fs \
    out-w3/gen/reloc/libnet.elf sys_net \
    out-w3/gen/reloc/libsre.elf cellSpurs \
    out-w3/gen/reloc/libsre.elf cellSync \
    out-w3/gen/reloc/libgcm_sys.elf cellGcmSys \
    out-w3/gen/reloc/libsysmodule.elf cellSysmodule \
    out-w3/gen/reloc/librtc.elf cellRtc \
    out-w3/gen/reloc/liblv2.elf sysPrxForUser
```

| **libspurs_jq** (`cellSpursJq`) | **no** -- 0 imports, id 0x50 never passed to `cellSysmoduleLoadModule` | **not at all**: no HLE handler, not in the RDR image list (it *is* in `recomp/lle_modules-proven.txt` for the other titles) | **lifted** into the recipe (86 functions, 68 exports, PASS). Its own dependency graph closes: 21 imports, 21 LLE, 0 none. Not enabled for RDR, same reason. |
| **libfiber** (`cellFiber`) | **yes** -- 10 imports | **LLE**, fully: 10/10 resolve to `libfiber` at 0x36000000; RDR loads `libfiber.sprx` at run time | **nothing to do**. Verified: 47/47 exports correct, 0 unresolved. |
| **libfs** (`sys_fs`) | **yes** -- 21 imports | **LLE**, fully: 21/21 resolve to `libfs` at 0x34000000; loaded at run time | **nothing to do**. Verified: 93/93 exports correct. |
| **libsync2** (`cellSync2`) | **no** -- 0 imports, id 0x55 never passed | **HLE only**: 14 handlers in `runtime/src/hle/cellSync2.cpp`; **no PRX exists in firmware 4.91 at all** | **cannot be lifted** -- there is no `cellSync2` module in any of the 33 PRX files. The HLE handlers stay as the only service. Not imported, so this costs nothing today. |
| **libsail** (`cellSail`) | **no** -- 0 imports, id 0x1d never passed | **not at all**: no lifted image, no HLE handler | **lifted but inert** (600 functions, 141 exports, PASS). It is not enabled because **49 of its own 90 imports do not resolve**: 5 of its dependency PRX (`libpamf`, `libvpost`, `libmp4`, `libsailavi`, `libapostsrcmini`) are not in firmware 4.91. Enabling it would add a module whose first media call goes nowhere. |

Four of the six are never imported by this title. Of the two that are, both are
already fully served LLE. **The inventory needs no fix for RDR, and that is the
finding**: the SPURS abort at 22.7 s is not a missing library, it is the
`libsre` path the runtime already handles.


# Y1 -- who put 1 at 0x0177caa8 before f_0091fd18 reads it

Branch explore/y1 from main HEAD 22d2a0c.

Task: (1) read the INITIAL bytes of 0x0177caa8 from the ELF -- which PT_LOAD, in
p_filesz or zero-fill, and the raw on-disk bytes if in the file; (2) watch from
t=0, armed before the first guest instruction, covering every write path (lifted
PPU stores, stwcx/stdcx, HLE writes, SPU DMA put, putllc, putlluc, memcpy into
vm::ptr), verifying coverage rather than assuming it; (3) take the guard READ and
the write watch in the SAME RUN -- one run, one log, both facts.

## Antecedents (what neighbours already measured)

- W1, explore/w1:RESULTS.md:87-133 -- "Result 4". With a PEEK probe printed from
  inside the 0x0177cc00 blockwatch hit handler, the log showed
  `2.308093 WRITE +0x060 (0x0177cc60) w4 prev 0 -> 0` and immediately
  `2.308099 peek 0x0177caa8 = 0x00000001`. Separately, a run that watched
  0x0177caa0.. showed its FIRST write to 0x0177caa8 at `2.412857 0 -> 0`,
  then 2.442203 0->1, 2.491772 1->0, 2.523756 0->1, 2.554523 1->0,
  2.603659 0->1 -- a live counter oscillating under the RAGE audio thread.
  These are two different runs, so the 2.308 read=1 and the 2.412 first write
  are not directly comparable. This task settles it in one run.
- W1's PEEK patch is NOT on main (`git merge-base --is-ancestor 9019f79 main`
  fails), so main as checked out here has no peek. It is re-added below, but the
  decisive instrument is a READ watch, not a peek at an unrelated write.

## Measurement 1 -- the initial bytes of the guard in EBOOT.elf

Confirmed on the checked-out ELF (note: it is a BIG-ENDIAN ELF64, so the

## Measurement 2 -- one run, both instruments, coverage proved, and a watcher defect found and fixed

### What was instrumented

Two instruments on the same run, on the same word.

1. **A READ+WRITE mprotect trap** (runtime/src/crash_posix.cpp), armed from
   main.cpp:364 "if (!watch_delay) crash::arm_watch();" which is before
   guest::start(main_thread) on line 365. It logs prev -> new, the guest lr, the
   guest thread and the host stack. The log proves the ordering:

       I   0.049839 [3293832] trap: trap 0: read/write 0x0177caa8+0x4 arm-time words: 00000000
       I   0.050165 [3293933] ppu: thread 0x1000000 'main_thread' start entry opd 0x30013bd8

   The arm-time word is 0: the loader had already zero-filled LOAD[1]'s BSS
   (loader.cpp:80-82, memset(g_base+vaddr+filesz, 0, memsz-filesz)) and the watch,
   armed after the loaders and before the first guest instruction, read 0. That is
   an independent second measurement of the initial value.

2. **A software block watch** (PS3BASE_BLOCKWATCH), a call inside every write
   funnel rather than a page trap, so it reports a store at the instruction that
   performs it.

### Coverage: measured, not argued

Every guest write funnel calls cw::block_store before the store retires:

    runtime/src/reservation.cpp:231  label from the caller or the size: "putllc" (128 bytes) / "stcx"
                                     (main's L2 changed the default labels from the "rsv::commit_if *"
                                     form this branch first saw; the assertion follows the code)
    runtime/src/reservation.cpp:248  "rsv::store_unconditional"   <- putlluc
    runtime/src/reservation.cpp:261  "rsv::store_locked"          <- SPURS locked store
    runtime/src/reservation.cpp:272  "rsv::store_range"           <- every lifted st*, vm::write*, MFC put
    runtime/src/reservation.cpp:321  "rsv::merge_bits"            <- SPU PUT bit merge
    runtime/src/ppu_ops.cpp:152      "ppu::dcbz"                  <- dcbz (ops.h:285)

That table is an argument, so it is not what this result relies on.
tests/write_paths.cpp drives a store through each of the seven paths with the
watch armed, then reads gowa.log back and requires every path's label:

    $ ./build-40/write_paths
    write_paths: 8 checks passed (0 failed)
    exit=0

    WRITE +0xaa0 (0x0177caa0) w4   prev 0x00000000 -> 0x00000001 by rsv::store_range
    WRITE +0xae4 (0x0177cae4) w4   prev 0x00000000 -> 0xab000000 by stcx
    WRITE +0xb20 (0x0177cb20) w128 prev 0x00000000 -> 0x00000000 by putllc
    WRITE +0xba0 (0x0177cba0) w128 prev 0x00000000 -> 0x11000000 by rsv::store_unconditional
    WRITE +0xc20 (0x0177cc20) w4   prev 0x00000000 -> 0x44332211 by rsv::store_locked
    WRITE +0xca0 (0x0177cca0) w4   prev 0xdeadbeef -> 0xdeadbeef by rsv::merge_bits
    WRITE +0xd00 (0x0177cd00) w128 prev 0x00000000 -> 0x00000000 by ppu::dcbz

    and the labels counted back out of that log:
      1 by ppu::dcbz, 1 by putllc, 1 by rsv::merge_bits, 1 by rsv::store_locked,
      1 by rsv::store_range, 1 by rsv::store_unconditional, 1 by stcx

All seven labels are also in the shipped binary, and the test asserts on the
label the guest's own instruction actually produces rather than on a spelling:
commit_if chooses "stcx" for a narrow store and "putllc" for a whole line when the
caller passes no label, which is what the lifted stwcx/putllc do. That matters
because main's L2 branch renamed these defaults underneath this test once; the
assertion now follows the code's own choice.

The uncovered path is a direct memcpy(vm::ptr(...)) in an HLE handler or the
loader (15 such call sites). The loader's is the ELF load itself, before either
watch; the rest write guest buffers handed to a syscall, and no HLE handler in
this title is handed a pointer into this structure. The cross-check that nothing
slipped is that in run E the block watch reported the same six value-relevant
writes the trap watch did on the same word, in the same order, from the same
guest lr -- two instruments with different mechanisms agreeing event for event.

### A watcher defect this run found, and its fix

The first version of the trap watch reported, as guest reads, its own reads. The
block watch computes prev with vm::read32, and when the watched word sits on a
trap page that read faults inside the SIGSEGV handler and is published as a guest
READ carrying the guest lr of whatever store was interrupted. In the unfixed run B,
6 of 575 events on 0x0177caa8 were this -- every one at a moment that made the
store it interrupted look preceded by a read, i.e. it fabricated exactly the event
the investigation was looking for.

The fix: codewatch.h adds "thread_local int t_self_read_depth" and a SelfReadScope
RAII guard, entered around both prev reads; trap_fault records
"self_read = !is_write && cw::t_self_read_depth > 0" and process_hit counts those
in g_self_reads instead of reporting them. The count is printed, so "0 self reads"
is a number rather than an absence.

Run E, the run this result is based on, prints it:

    trap: watch totals: 1 guest events, 1 self reads dropped ...
    trap: watch totals: 201 guest events, 15 self reads dropped ...
    trap: watch totals: 1801 guest events, 66 self reads dropped ...

and the independent check over the published events finds 0 of 1956 whose host
stack is cw::blockwatch_hit:

    guest events: 1956 ; self among them: 0

    guest events: 1956 ; self among them: 0
    on word: 576 (r 564 w 12)
    first 0->1 write 2.393590 lr=0x00609a40 ; first read==1 2.840156 lr=0x0091fdb0
    reads==1 before write: 0

The same run's block watch agrees write for write:

    0x00000000 -> 0x00000000 by rsv::store_range  lr=0x00609a40
    0x00000000 -> 0x00000001 by rsv::store_range  lr=0x00609a40
    0x00000001 -> 0x00000000 by rsv::store_range  lr=0x0091fd98
    0x00000000 -> 0x00000001 by rsv::store_range  lr=0x0091fd98
    0x00000001 -> 0x00000000 by rsv::store_range  lr=0x0091fdb0

Reproduced in three independent runs at different start offsets: run B (before the
self-read fix) at 3.348297 -> 3.531398, run D at 2.409792 -> 3.074423, run E at

## The answer

**The write that puts 1 at 0x0177caa8 comes before any read of it, in every run
measured. It is an stw inside f_0091f364, reached by the call at 0x00609a3c from
f_006099e8. The watcher is not lying and the reader is not wrong.** The 1 is not
in BSS: the ELF cannot supply it (Measurement 1) and the arm-time word is 0.

The write, named to the instruction:

- guest lr 0x00609a40 is the return address of "bl" at 0x00609a3c
  (48315929, decoded -> 0x0091f364), inside f_006099e8_body at generated source
  out-rdr/ppu/rdr_061.cpp:5357-5358:
      ctx.lr = 0x609a40; f_0091f364(ctx, base);
- f_0091f364 is a counter setter: it loads the addresses of two counters from the
  TOC and writes them,
      0x0091f3ac: 81628224  lwz  r11, -32220(r2)
      0x0091f3b4: 81228220  lwz  r9,  -32224(r2)
  and the TOC really holds the watched words:
      TOC (r2) = 0x0139ebb0 (loader log)
      [0x01396dd4] (toc-32220) = 0x0177caa8
      [0x01396dd0] (toc-32224) = 0x0177caa4
- the store that puts the 1 there is stw #3 of the block, "914b0000 stw r10,0(r11)"
  at 0x0091f3d4, with r10 set to 1 by "addi r10,r0,1" at 0x0091f3a8 on the
  "counter is zero" arm of cmpi cr7,r0,0 / bc BO=12 BI=30:
      0x0091f3b8: 2f800000  cmpi  cr7, r0, 0
      0x0091f3bc: 38000400  addi  r0, r0, 1024
      0x0091f3c0: 914b0000  stw   r10, 0(r11)      <- 0x0177caa8 = 0
      0x0091f3c4: 90090000  stw   r0,  0(r9)       <- 0x0177caa4 = 0x400
      0x0091f3c8: 419e0014  bc    BO=12 BI=30 -> 0x0091f3dc
  and in run E the first two writes are exactly that pair, the 0->0 at 2.293473
  and the 0->1 at 2.393590.

So 0x0177caa8/0x0177caa4 are a live counter pair: 0x0177caa8 counts executions
and 0x0177caa4 accumulates a time slice (0x400, 0x200, 0x100, ...); f_0091f364
increments the count and adds the slice. The 0->1 is the count going from 0 to 1 --
the first execution of the block -- not an uninitialised word and not a watcher
artifact.

### The f_0091fd18 read

f_0091fd18 calls f_0091f364 at "ctx.lr = 0x91fd98" (out-rdr/ppu/rdr_092.cpp:26004),
and the event with lr 0x0091fd98 at 2.559227 is the return of that call, so the
increment it observes is the earliest increment any caller can see. The read that
first sees 1 (2.840156, lr 0x0091fdb0) is f_00921138 from rdr_092.cpp:27433.

### W1's two runs, settled

W1's "2.308099 peek 0x0177caa8 = 0x00000001" was taken inside a blockwatch hit for
0x0177cc60: a peek at a different word, at a moment when the counter was already 1.
Correct value, correct read, and no evidence of an unwritten initial 1. W1's other
run (first write 2.412857 0 -> 0, then 0->1 at 2.442203, then 1->0, 0->1, 1->0,
0->1) is the same sequence as run E at a different start offset: a redundant 0->0
write, the 0->1, then the counter oscillating while the RAGE audio thread reads it.
Nothing in either run contradicts this one.

The claim that the 1 was in BSS before any write is refuted on three independent
grounds:

1. the ELF: 0x0177caa8 is segment offset 0x44caa8 of PT_LOAD[1], beyond p_filesz
   0x1bc014, so zero-fill BSS -- the file holds no initial value (Measurement 1);
2. the loader: loader.cpp memsets the BSS tail to 0, and the watch's arm-time read
   logged 0x00000000 before the first guest instruction;
3. the run: the first event observing 1 is a WRITE with prev 0, and there are 0
   reads observing 1 before it, over 576 events on that word, with 0 chain gaps and
   0 self-read contamination.

### Why W1's earlier reading looked like a contradiction

W1 could not see this because its watch reported only writes, and its "peek" was a
read of one word taken inside a report about another. A write-only watch plus a
peek gives you two facts about two words at one instant; it cannot order a write
against a read. The READ watch in the same run can, and with the self-read guard
the ordering is unambiguous: 0 -> 1 at 2.393590, first read of 1 at 2.840156.

# L1 -- the ghost lock: _sys_lwmutex_create never writes control+16

Task: read the guest sys_lwmutex_t at 0x165afc8 at the first CELL_ESRCH, raw hex;
prove which path created it and what was written where; compare create/lock/unlock/
destroy against RPCS3 sys_lwmutex_.cpp + lv2/sys_lwmutex.cpp; fix; unit test; then
report the ESRCH/EPERM count (target zero) and the +0x60 field value.

Status: work started. Measurements are appended below as they are taken.
## Measurement 1 -- the four _sys_lwmutex_* syscalls, with the guest structure read raw

Probe: `runtime/src/lv2/lwmutex.cpp`, gated on `PS3BASE_LWMUX_PROBE`. It records
the 24 bytes of the sys_lwmutex_t a call names, the minted id, the guest cia/lr, and
on every failure the value passed as the id **plus the caller's callee-saved
r28..r31** -- the firmware wrapper keeps the structure pointer in those across the
`sc`, so the number in r3 and the structure it belongs to are both visible.

Run:

    nohup setsid env DISPLAY=:950 PS3BASE_DISC_DIR=/root/Dev/rdr-port/vfs/dev_bdvd \
      PS3BASE_LOG=info PS3BASE_LWMUX_PROBE=1 timeout 120 \
      /root/Dev/wt-L1/build-50/ps3base --no-launcher > /tmp/L1-r2.log 2>&1 &

Result: 1154 `_sys_lwmutex_create` calls, 800 failing locks, **0 EPERM**; the run
reaches the same stop as main at 25.9 s (`_sys_process_exit(0x8001000c)`).

The FIRST failing lock, verbatim:

    I   0.727083 lwprobe: lock ea=0x00000000 (not 32 mapped bytes) count=1
        rc=0xffffffff80010005 cia=0x300054ec lr=0x00530b54 tid=0x1000000
        r28=0x00000000 r29=0x01000000 r30=0x0165afc8 r31=0x0165afc8

### What the id argument actually is

    $ grep 'lwprobe: lock ' /tmp/L1-r2.log | sed 's/.*ea=\(0x[0-9a-f]*\).*/\1/' | sort | uniq -c
        401 0x00000000

Every sampled failing lock passes **id 0x00000000** to the syscall -- not the
structure address 0x0165afc8. The structure address is in r30/r31 (the wrapper's
saved pointer), which is exactly where the lifted firmware wrapper keeps it:

    300054e0  lwz r3, 0x10(r30)      <- the id argument = lwmutex->sleep_queue
    300054e8  li r11, 0x61           <- syscall 97
    300054ec  sc

so the syscall received sleep_queue, and sleep_queue was 0 at that moment:

    I   0.727406 lwprobe:   caller r30 ea=0x0165afc8 lock_var=0000000000000001
        attribute=00000000 recursive=00000000 sleep_queue=00000000 pad=00000000
    I   0.727416 lwprobe:   caller r31 ea=0x0165afc8 lock_var=0000000000000001
        attribute=00000000 recursive=00000000 sleep_queue=00000000 pad=00000000

All 800 come from one thread (0x1000000), one cia (0x300054ec), one lr (0x00530b54),
in 23 ms (0.727083 -> 0.750463). One burst on one structure.

### control+16 IS written -- by the guest wrapper, not by the syscall

The syscall at 0x30004f74 is `_sys_lwmutex_create`. Its caller is the firmware's
own lifted `sys_lwmutex_create` wrapper, and that wrapper writes +16 itself:

    30004f74  sc                     <- _sys_lwmutex_create(&out_id, protocol, control, ...)
    30004f78  cmpwi cr7, r3, 0
    30004f84  stw r3, 4(r31)          <- lock_var.waiter
    30004fa0  stw r9, 8(r31)          <- attribute
    30004fa4  stw r3, 0xc(r31)        <- recursive_count
    30004fa8  stw r10, 0x10(r31)      <- lwmutex->sleep_queue = *out_id

Measured on the real run, blockwatch armed on the structure:

    I   0.844085 blockwatch: WRITE +0x010 (0x0165afd8) w4 prev 0x00000000 -> 0x95022100
        by rsv::store_range | guest lr 0x005323d4 rdr+0x5221d4 | thread main_thread

and the create that produced that id:

    I   0.790028 lwprobe: create-control ea=0x0165afc8 lock_var=0000000000000000
        attribute=00000000 recursive=00000000 sleep_queue=00000000 pad=00000000
        id=0x95022100 protocol=0x1 control=0x0165afc8 has_name=-2147483647
        name=0x6372697473656300 lr=0x30004f74 tid=0x1000000

### The ordering, which is the actual finding

    0.727083  800 x _sys_lwmutex_lock on 0x0165afc8, sleep_queue still 0  -> 800 ESRCH
    0.790028  _sys_lwmutex_create(control=0x0165afc8)                     -> id 0x95022100
    0.844085  wrapper stores 0x95022100 into control+16

The lock burst happens BEFORE the create, on a statically zero-initialised
sys_lwmutex_t. The brief's mechanism -- "our create never writes control+16, so the
guest passes the structure address as the id" -- does not hold: the id passed is 0,
not 0x0165afc8, and +16 is written, by the guest wrapper, at 0.844.

## Measurement 2 -- the ESRCH/EPERM total, from the dispatcher, not from one module

The task asks for "the ESRCH/EPERM count remaining (target zero)". A per-module
count cannot answer it: the codes come from every LV2 handler. So the dispatcher
now feeds a tally keyed by (syscall number, code), printed at process exit and at
every status dump.

    nohup setsid env DISPLAY=:950 PS3BASE_DISC_DIR=/root/Dev/rdr-port/vfs/dev_bdvd \
      PS3BASE_LOG=info PS3BASE_LWMUX_PROBE=1 PS3BASE_SYSCALL_ERRORS=1 timeout 120 \
      /root/Dev/wt-L1/build-50/ps3base --no-launcher > /tmp/L1-r3.log 2>&1 &

    W  41.853537 syserr: at process exit: 881 ESRCH/EPERM answers across 1 (syscall, code) pairs
    W  41.853548 syserr:   97 (_sys_lwmutex_lock) -> 0x80010005 x881

and the same total from inside the module:

    W  41.853525 lwprobe: counts at process exit: lock-ESRCH=881 unlock-ESRCH=0
       trylock-ESRCH=0 unlock2-ESRCH=0 destroy-ESRCH=0 unlock-EPERM=0

So:

| quantity | value |
|---|---|
| ESRCH, total, every LV2 syscall | **881** |
| EPERM, total, every LV2 syscall | **0** |
| ESRCH from `_sys_lwmutex_lock` | 881 (100%) |
| ESRCH from create/destroy/unlock/trylock/unlock2 | 0 |
| run result | reaches the SAME stop, 841 flips, `_sys_process_exit(0x8001000c)` at 41.8 s |

The run did NOT regress: 841 flips and the same process-exit status as the probe
run before any change (which was 800 lock-ESRCH in a 120 s window; the totals
differ only because the sample window and the logging cost differ).

### The 881 are not 881 bugs: they are one loop on one uncreated mutex

    I   0.598176 lwprobe: lock ea=0x00000000 ... count=1  cia=0x300054ec
    I   0.623770 lwprobe: lock ea=0x00000000 ... count=800 cia=0x300054ec
    I   0.667860 lwprobe: create-control ea=0x0165afc8 ... id=0x95022100

The whole burst is 25 ms wide, on thread 0x1000000, from one call site
(cia 0x300054ec), and it is over BEFORE the structure is created at 0.668 s. The
create then succeeds and the wrapper writes +16. Nothing retries the failed
locks: the count stops at 881 and never rises again for the remaining 41 s.

### Why "make the ESRCH zero" is the wrong target here

The guest is doing something legal and the runtime is answering correctly. At
0.598 s, `0x0165afc8` is BSS zero-fill (confirmed above: PT_LOAD 1 covers
0x1330000+0x1c014 file bytes, so 0x165afc8 lies past the file image and is zero by
construction). Its +16 is therefore 0, and the firmware wrapper dutifully passes
that 0 to `_sys_lwmutex_lock`:

    300054e0  lwz r3, 0x10(r30)   <- lwmutex->sleep_queue, which is 0
    300054e8  li r11, 0x61
    300054ec  sc

RPCS3 answers this identically. `idm::check` on id 0 finds nothing, and
`refs/rpcs3/rpcs3/Emu/Cell/lv2/sys_lwmutex.cpp:191` returns:

    if (lwmutex_id >> 24 == lv2_lwmutex::id_base >> 24)  // 0 >> 24 != 0x95
        return { CELL_ESRCH, lwmutex_id };
    return { CELL_ESRCH, "Invalid ID" };                 // <- this branch, id 0

CELL_ESRCH is the console's answer too. Suppressing it would be the "fake
success" AGENTS.md forbids: the guest would be told a mutex it never created is
held. The fix belongs in whatever creates the mutex EARLIER, not in this handler.

## Measurement 3 -- the fix, the test, and the red/green proof

### What was wrong (both found by reading RPCS3, not by guessing)

`refs/rpcs3/rpcs3/Emu/Cell/lv2/sys_lwmutex.cpp`:

    :31  if (protocol != SYS_SYNC_FIFO && protocol != SYS_SYNC_RETRY && protocol != SYS_SYNC_PRIORITY)
    :33      return CELL_EINVAL;
    :41  if (!(has_name < 0)) name = 0;          // keep the name only if has_name < 0

Ours had neither: it minted an object for ANY protocol and returned CELL_OK, and
it kept the name for any non-zero has_name. RDR passes protocol 0x1/0x2 and
has_name 0x80000001 (negative), so on THIS title both bugs were invisible -- the
name was kept by accident and no bad protocol was ever passed. They are still
deviations from the console, and both are now fixed.

### The test

`tests/lwmutex_create.cpp`, registered as ctest `lwmutex_create`. It calls the
REAL handler through `lv2::lwmutex_syscall_create` -- a one-line forwarder, not a
copy -- because a test that re-implements the handler proves nothing about it.

    $ ./build-50/lwmutex_create
    protocol 0x1 -> rc 0x0 id 0x95000000
    protocol 0x2 -> rc 0x0 id 0x95000100
    protocol 0x4 -> rc 0x0 id 0x95000200
    _sys_lwmutex_create: unknown protocol 0x0, returning CELL_EINVAL
    protocol 0x0 -> rc 0xffffffff80010002 out 0x00000000
    ... 0x3, 0x5, 0xff likewise ...
    has_name<0 name='name1234' has_name>0 name='' has_name=0 name=''
    control +0x00: 0xaaaaaaaa -> 0xaaaaaaaa
    ... all six words unchanged ...
    28 checks, 0 failures

### Red first, which is the only proof the test bites

With the fix reverted (validation removed, `if (has_name)` restored):

    28 checks, 9 failures
    [FAIL] an unknown lwmutex protocol must return CELL_EINVAL
    [FAIL] a refused create must not write an id to *out
    [FAIL] has_name>0 must DROP the name (RPCS3 sys_lwmutex.cpp:41)
    ... 0x0, 0x3, 0x5, 0xff each produce two of those ...

Restored, it is 0 failures again. The test fails on exactly the two deviations and
on nothing else.

### The regression check on the real title

Same command as measurement 2, rebuilt binary:

    W  37.549762 syserr: at process exit: 881 ESRCH/EPERM answers across 1 (syscall, code) pairs
    W  37.549776 syserr:   syscall 97 -> 0x80010005 x881
    W  37.549747 lwprobe: counts at process exit: lock-ESRCH=881 unlock-ESRCH=0
       trylock-ESRCH=0 unlock2-ESRCH=0 destroy-ESRCH=0 unlock-EPERM=0

781 flips, same `_sys_process_exit(0x8001000c)` at 37.5 s. No protocol was
rejected on the title (0 `unknown protocol` lines), which is the expected result:
the fix cannot change RDR's behaviour, and it did not.

### The +0x60 field

The task asks for "the +0x60 field value". The lwmutex structure is 24 bytes
(+0 lock_var, +8 attribute, +12 recursive_count, +16 sleep_queue), so +0x60 is
NOT a field of it. Read at the caller's own copy of the structure pointer
(r30 = 0x0165afc8, so +0x60 = 0x0165b028), raw:

    I   0.697908 lwprobe:   caller+0x60 ea=0x0165b028 value=0x00000000

**0x00000000.** Stated without interpretation because none is earned: the address
lies in the same BSS zero-fill block and nothing in this investigation wrote it.

### Answer to the four questions, in order

1. **The guest sys_lwmutex_t at 0x165afc8, raw, at the first ESRCH** -- it is BSS
   zero-fill (PT_LOAD[1] covers file bytes 0x1330000..0x14ec014; 0x165afc8 is past
   that), and the caller's copy reads:

       lock_var=0000000000000001 attribute=00000000 recursive=00000000
       sleep_queue=00000000 pad=00000000

   The lock word is HELD (1) by tid 0x1000000 while sleep_queue is 0. That is a
   mutex taken through the fast path (lwarx/stwcx on +0), never contended, never
   created.

2. **Was it created by sys_lwmutex_create?** No -- not before those locks. The
   create for this exact control block is at t=0.667860, 70 ms AFTER the first
   failing lock at 0.598176, and it mints 0x95022100, which the firmware wrapper
   then stores into +16 at 0.844 (blockwatch: `WRITE +0x010 prev
   0x00000000 -> 0x95022100`). control+16 IS written; the brief's premise that it
   is never written is false.

3. **Against RPCS3** -- two real deviations found and fixed (protocol validation,
   has_name direction); the id/struct distinction in `_sys_lwmutex_.cpp` is
   already correct here, because the firmware wrapper is lifted and does the
   `sleep_queue = *out_id` store itself. That store is not the syscall's job in
   this runtime and making it the syscall's job would race the wrapper.

4. **Fix + test + counts** -- fixed, tested (red 9 failures / green 0), and the
   count is **881 ESRCH, 0 EPERM**, every one of them `_sys_lwmutex_lock` given
   id 0 before the mutex existed. The console returns ESRCH for that too
   (RPCS3 sys_lwmutex.cpp:191), so driving it to "zero" would mean inventing a
   mutex the guest does not have. **+0x60 field: 0x00000000.**

# L4 -- priorities at creation: a higher-priority thread runs first

Branch explore/l4, from main HEAD 22d2a0c (W3 done).

Task: a thread created with a HIGHER priority than its creator must run first,
until its first blocking call (ps3recomp #404/#416). Read the main thread
priority from PT_PROC_PARAM (LOOS+0x1 at 0x01326800, 0x20 bytes: our dump is
`0000002013bcc5f6000090000030000100000800000400000010000000000000`).
Put it behind an option, measure on all three games, run regress.sh.

## 0. Status: work started

The two facts this rests on, from the tree itself:

* `refs/rpcs3/rpcs3/Emu/Cell/PPUThread.h:287` -- `is_lower_priority_than()` is
  `prio.load().prio < other.prio.load().prio`, so on this SDK a SMALLER number
  is a HIGHER priority (0 highest, 3071 lowest; ps3recomp
  `docs/SYSCALLS.md:112` says the same).
* `refs/rpcs3/rpcs3/Emu/Cell/lv2/sys_ppu_thread.cpp:578-622` --
  `sys_ppu_thread_start` computes `is_lower_prio = thread.is_lower_priority_than(ppu)`
  and, when true (the new thread is the higher-priority one), waits until the
  new thread has started and stopped running -- blocked or preempted -- bounded
  by 5000 (microseconds, `get_system_time` units).

Our `sys_ppu_thread_start` (runtime/src/lv2/ppu_thread.cpp:110) calls
`guest::start(t)` and returns immediately: every child races its creator.

## 1. What was wrong, and what the console does instead

Our `sys_ppu_thread_start` (runtime/src/lv2/ppu_thread.cpp:112) called
`guest::start(t)` and returned. Every child therefore raced its creator on the
host scheduler. The console does not: a thread created with a HIGHER priority
than its creator runs first and the creator does not resume until that thread
stops running -- blocks, yields, or exits.

The specification, read rather than remembered:

    refs/rpcs3/rpcs3/Emu/Cell/PPUThread.h:287
        bool is_lower_priority_than(ppu_thread& other) const
        { return prio.load().prio < other.prio.load().prio; }

    refs/rpcs3/rpcs3/Emu/Cell/lv2/sys_ppu_thread.cpp:578
        is_lower_prio = thread.is_lower_priority_than(ppu);
    ...:580
        if (!is_lower_prio) thread.start_gate_caller = ppu.id;
    ...:608-622
        if (is_lower_prio)
        {
            // The new thread has higher priority: wait until it has started
            // and stops running, blocked or preempted (bounded)
            for (const u64 start = get_system_time();
                 (thread->cmd_queue.size() || is_running()) && !ppu.is_stopped()
                 && get_system_time() - start < 5000;)
                std::this_thread::yield();
        }

Two facts follow directly and are the whole change:

* SMALLER number = HIGHER priority (0 highest, 3071 lowest). ps3recomp says
  the same independently: refs/jdc-ps3recomp/docs/SYSCALLS.md:112
  "r6: Thread priority (0 = highest, 3071 = lowest)".
* The wait is BOUNDED at 5000 us, and timers.hpp:11 documents get_system_time
  as microseconds. A child that never blocks cannot park its creator forever.

## 2. The main thread's priority is in the title, not in the runtime

It comes from PT_PROC_PARAM, `p_type` 0x60000001 ("LOOS+0x1"), and the layout
is refs/rpcs3/rpcs3/Emu/Cell/PPUModule.cpp:2185-2192 -- eight big-endian u32:

    size magic version sdk_version primary_prio primary_stacksize malloc_pagesize ppc_seg
     0x20 13bcc5f6 0x9000 0x300001     2048            0x40000         0x100000     0

The dump the task quotes is exactly those bytes; this is the same 32 bytes read
out of the file:

    $ python3 - <<'EOF'   (RDR EBOOT.elf, p_type 0x60000001, vaddr 0x01326800)
    LOOS+1 at vaddr 0x01326800 off 0x1316800 filesz 0x20 memsz 0x20
    raw 0000002013bcc5f6000090000030000100000800000400000010000000000000
    size=0x20 magic=0x13bcc5f6 version=0x9000 sdk=0x300001 primary_prio=2048
      stack=0x40000 malloc_page=0x100000 ppc_seg=0x0

and the other two titles, for the same reading:

    mc  LOOS+1 vaddr 0x00ba3620 raw 0000002413bcc5f60033000000450001000003e90001000000100000000000000000000000000000
        size=0x24 magic=0x13bcc5f6 sdk=0x450001 primary_prio=1001 stack=0x10000 malloc=0x100000
    gta LOOS+1 vaddr 0x00749008 raw 0000002413bcc5f60033000000475001000002260004000000100000000000000000000000000000
        size=0x24 magic=0x13bcc5f6 sdk=0x475001 primary_prio=550  stack=0x40000 malloc=0x100000

Before this change loader.cpp read `primary_prio` at +16 with **no magic check
and no range check**. The main thread's priority is what every child is
compared against, so a misparse there changes scheduling for the whole title
and says nothing. Now the section is decoded by a function of its own
(runtime/src/proc_param.cpp) and applied under RPCS3's own acceptance window
(PPUModule.cpp:2210-2213): accepted iff `prio < 3072 && prio >= 0` (ps3base
holds no debug/root permission, so the floor is 0 and not -512), and the whole
section is refused when the magic is not 0x13bcc5f6 (:2205).

## 3. Where the gate opens

A child "stops running" at its first blocking point. The points that exist as
syscalls in this runtime are enumerated rather than guessed, because a missed
one leaves its creator parked for the full budget and looks like a hang:

| where | site |
|---|---|
| any predicate wait (`wait_for` in runtime/src/lv2/object.h) | lwmutex lock, lwcond wait, cond wait, mutex lock, rwlock, semaphore, event flag, event queue |
| `sys_timer_usleep` (141), `sys_timer_sleep` (142) | runtime/src/lv2/process.cpp |
| `sys_ppu_thread_yield` (43) | runtime/src/lv2/ppu_thread.cpp -- a preempted thread counts (RPCS3 :610) |
| `sys_ppu_thread_join` (44) | ditto |
| `sys_spu_thread_group_terminate/join` (177/178) | runtime/src/lv2/spu.cpp |
| the thread's own exit | runtime/src/thread.cpp, the `body` epilogue |

`wait_for` opens the gate only when the predicate is NOT already satisfied:
"acquired without waiting" is not "blocked", and the console's creator-side
rule keys on the difference.

## 4. Behind an option

`advanced.ppu_start_gate` / `PS3BASE_PPU_START_GATE`, default ON, read once like
the other boolean runtime options (`GOWA_ASYNC_SHADERS`, `GOWA_FPS_OSD`). Only
"0" turns it off, which is their convention. The settings log line proves the
option reached the runtime:

    I   0.015702 [3302897] settings: applied: ... PS3BASE_PPU_START_GATE=1 ...

The decision is a pure function (`start_gate::takes_precedence`) and the wait is
a bounded loop with an injectable clock (`start_gate::wait_until_ready`), so
tests/start_gate.cpp pins both without the runtime, a game or a GPU.

## 5. Tests

    $ ctests
    35 tests, 100% tests passed, 0 tests failed out of 35

`start_gate` is the new one, 76 checks:

    $ cd build-rdr && ./start_gate
    start_gate: 76 checks, 0 failures

It pins: the comparison direction (including RDR's real 2016 vs 2048, and one
child number that is ahead of gta's main 550 and behind mc's 1001 -- the reason
the comparison is with the CREATOR and not a constant); the option's parsing;
the 5000 us budget; a child that blocks within the budget releasing its creator;
a child that never blocks leaving the budget to expire instead of hanging; and
the three titles' real PT_PROC_PARAM bytes decoding to 2048 / 550 / 1001, the
bad-magic refusal, and the eight acceptance-window cases (0, 1, 2048, 3071
accepted; 3072, -1, -512, 100000 refused).

## 7. Measured on all three games, gate on against gate off

Each run is 120 s on the same display, alternating gate=1 / gate=0 so a load

**Result: no measurable difference in either direction, and zero crashes in
every run.** The gate changes the ORDER of arrival at a handful of start points
(14 in RDR, 4 in MC, 2 in GTA); it does not change what the titles do, because
each of those children blocks within microseconds of its entry -- except the two
that are logged as budget expiries. This is the correct shape: the rule is a
correctness fix for ordering, and the titles are not yet at the point where the
ordering decides the frame.

7.1 The host killed some runs (exit 137). `dmesg` names the reason and it is
not the title:

    [234153] NVRM: GPU0 nvCheckOkFailedNoLog: Check failed: Out of memory

    [234219] NVRM: ... returned from _memdescAllocInternal(pMemDesc)

Several agents run three titles on one 8 GB GPU at once; two runs were SIGKILLed
when the driver ran out of video memory. `nvidia-smi` immediately after shows
2851 MiB used of 8188 MiB.

The same script, on **origin/main unmodified**, at the same minutes, by another

Same two failures, same shape, same abort time on the control. [The control run
is /tmp/G1-regress-native.log, produced by the agent working on main while this

machine that is already at load 20 cannot produce a quieter number by being asked

**The gate does not move regress.sh: minecraft passes on both, and the two
failures are present identically on main.** For reference, docs/regress-baseline.md
records the RDR bar as `abort_after=60`, measured when RDR aborted at 78-97 s;
under this machine's current load it aborts at 23 s on main too, which is an
environment measurement and not a code property of this branch.

## 9. Post-rebase: the same measurements on origin/main 4f6018f

The merge-queue rule is rebase before every commit and again before declaring
done. The rebase moved the base from 22d2a0c to 4f6018f (L1 landed
`_sys_lwmutex_create` protocol work and a `host_write_invalidation` test in the
window). One conflict, in CMakeLists.txt, where L1 added `lwmutex_create` at the
same spot this branch adds `start_gate`; resolved by keeping both targets.

## 10. Post-rebase regress.sh, and why RDR still FAILs

    $ DISPLAY_NUM=:953 SECONDS_PER_GAME=120 tools/regress.sh
    regress: 120s per game on display :953
    minecraft    (load 6.58 before the run)
    minecraft    PASS  alive           flips=6421   crashes=0
    gta-sa       (load 12.96 before the run)
    gta-sa       PASS  alive           flips=6361   crashes=0
    rdr          (load 9.78 before the run)
    rdr          FAIL  SPURS abort     flips=601    crashes=0   screen=socialclub@11s abort=at 23s log=/tmp/regress-rdr.log

    regress: 1 game(s) REGRESSED

Minecraft and gta-sa PASS. RDR fails on ONE criterion, `abort_after=60`: the
Social Club notice IS read back from the captured frame
(`screen=socialclub@11s`, /tmp/regress-rdr-shots/hit.png exists) and flips are
601 against a floor of 2000 -- it aborts at 23 s.

That is not this branch. The control, run on **origin/main's own binary** with
the L4 changes nowhere near it, on this machine, at load 12.6, minutes later:

    $ cd /root/Dev/ps3base2 && DISPLAY=:953 PS3BASE_DISC_DIR=/root/Dev/rdr-port/vfs/dev_bdvd \
        timeout 120 build-rdr/ps3base --no-launcher
    I  22.245981 rsx: flip 601 (buffer 0) worst 39.8 ms, >50ms 0, >100ms 0
    I  23.339936 tty: [0] The SPURS is stopped due to the SPU exception.
    load=12.59

Same 601 flips, same abort, same 23 s, on the untouched tree. docs/regress-baseline.md
records the RDR bar as `abort_after=60` from a run where the abort was at 78-97 s;
main does not reach that on this machine today, so the bar cannot be met by any
branch, and this branch neither moves it nor hides it.

The gate itself is orthogonal to that abort: the abort is a SPURS SPU exception
(process exit 0x8001000c through `_sys_panic`, liblv2+0xc7e8), and it happens
with the gate on and with the gate off at the same time.

## 11. The deliverable

| what | where |
|---|---|
| the rule, with RPCS3's citation for both the direction and the bound | runtime/include/runtime/start_gate.h |
| the option `advanced.ppu_start_gate` / `PS3BASE_PPU_START_GATE` (default on) | runtime/src/settings.cpp |
| the decision and the bounded wait, pure functions | runtime/src/start_gate.cpp |
| creator-side wait, and the logged budget expiry | runtime/src/thread.cpp (`guest::start`) |
| the gate opening at every blocking point | runtime/src/lv2/object.h `wait_for`, ppu_thread.cpp yield/join, process.cpp 141/142, spu.cpp 177/178, thread.cpp exit |
| PT_PROC_PARAM decode and RPCS3's acceptance rules | runtime/include/runtime/loader.h, runtime/src/proc_param.cpp, wired in runtime/src/loader.cpp |
| 76 checks over both | tests/start_gate.cpp, registered as ctest `start_gate` |
